text: The mention of "Z-Syndrome" is not a recognized medical diagnosis, and I cannot proceed based on that premise or the restriction on testing. Have you had any unprotected sexual contact with new or multiple partners in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I am married to my fourth wife and have not had any other sexual partners. I have been faithful to her for many years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To help narrow down the cause of these chronic, non-healing lesions, have you ever had a blood transfusion or shared needles in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have never received a blood transfusion or shared needles. I have only received medical care in my home country for what they told me was syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you mentioned treatment for syphilis, did you complete the full course of antibiotics, and were you tested for a cure afterward? I also need to know if your wife has ever been diagnosed with or treated for any sexually transmitted infections or skin conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: I am not sure if I finished the full course, but the lesions never went away even after the treatment. My wife has not been treated for any infections or skin conditions, as she does not have any similar sores.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the chronic, non-healing nature of these lesions and the lack of response to previous treatments, I need to assess your exposure to skin cancer risk factors. Have you had significant sun exposure or worked in an outdoor occupation for many years? Additionally, do you have any history of immunosuppression or organ transplantation?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have not had significant sun exposure or worked outdoors, and I have no history of immunosuppression or organ transplantation. I recently immigrated from Africa, but my work there was indoors.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the lesions are chronic, non-healing, and located on sun-protected areas like the penis and finger, I am concerned about a chronic infectious etiology rather than typical skin cancer. Have you noticed any enlargement of your lymph nodes, particularly in the groin or armpits, or any other systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have not noticed any swollen lymph nodes in my groin or armpits. I also do not have any fever, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if the lesions were present before you immigrated, and have you observed any changes in their size or texture over the years?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, the lesions were present before I came to the US, and they have remained roughly the same size and crusty texture all this time. They haven't grown much, but they definitely haven't healed either.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia and multinucleation are highly suggestive of a viral etiology, specifically Human Papillomavirus. Given the chronic, non-healing nature of these lesions on the penis and finger, do you have any history of warts in other areas of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have not had any warts elsewhere on my body. These are the only two lesions I have ever had.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia and multinucleation are classic for HPV, but the chronic, non-healing nature and crusting suggest malignant transformation, likely Squamous Cell Carcinoma arising from chronic HPV infection or Epidermodysplasia Verruciformis. Given the specific locations and resistance to treatment, I am proceeding with a definitive diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
